extracted.intended_audience: media, partner organizations, journalists, donors, volunteers, and other interested members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: Brand and messaging guidelines for producing media materials (press releases, stories, social posts) about Habitat for Humanity Capital Region, including proper names, program descriptions, tone, and contact/social info. Focused on accurate, consistent, and non-misleading representation of the organization's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper name usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use “Habitat for Humanity Capital Region” when being referred to for the first time. “Habitat Capital Region” can be used after the full name has been used. Never use just “Habitat” or “Habitat for Humanity” to refer to Habitat Capital Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shorter forms refer only to the parent organization (Habitat for Humanity International). Always introduce the full legal/brand name on first reference in press materials, then you may use the shortened local name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not say we give away homes
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitat for Humanity Capital Region does NOT give away homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate that Habitat works in partnership with homeowners who contribute hours of sweat equity and pay an affordable mortgage. Emphasize partnership, contribution, and homebuyer responsibility rather than charity or free giveaways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer/partner framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteers, donors, and supporters build homes with homeowners, NOT for homeowners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that shows collaboration (e.g., 'build with') to reflect the mutual effort and to avoid portraying homeowners as passive recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who to call program participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to program participants as “partners”, “homebuyers”, or “clients” NOT “families”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Habitat serves both families and individuals; calling everyone 'families' perpetuates a misconception and can misrepresent the diversity of participants. Use partner/homebuyer/client to be inclusive and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homeownership Program messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the Homeownership Program as constructing new homes and renovating existing homes alongside Habitat homebuyers with the support of community partners, donors, and volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that the program is designed to lower barriers to affordable homeownership and create opportunities for those who may not otherwise have access. Use active, partnership-focused language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Home Repair Program messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: State that the Critical Home Repair Program addresses critical exterior repair needs for low- to moderate-income homeowners in Clinton, Eaton, and Ingham Counties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight that repairs help homeowners maintain home integrity, prevent further deterioration, and enable people to live in safe, affordable homes for years to come.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ramp Program messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain that the Ramp Program serves anyone in the Capital Region who needs a ramp and meets basic program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify eligibility broadly (renters, homeowners, people in mobile homes can qualify) to avoid unintentional exclusionary language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer Program messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey that volunteers are crucial to making homeownership affordable and that Habitat Capital Region creates meaningful volunteer opportunities for individuals, groups, and corporate team-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this messaging to recruit and thank volunteers; highlight the meaningful nature of opportunities and the impact of volunteer labor on affordability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat ReStore messaging and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the Habitat for Humanity Capital Region ReStores (locations: Lansing, St Johns, Williamston) as nonprofit thrift stores and donation centers whose proceeds help build and repair local homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate that donating and shopping at ReStores supports local builds/repairs, provides an affordable avenue for home improvement, and diverts usable items from landfills. Use full ReStore name on first reference and location-specific mentions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding/subsidy explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain that Habitat Capital Region subsidizes services based on client income to create equitable access and that to cover the 'subsidy gap' the organization operates ReStores, applies for grants, solicits donations, builds partnerships, hosts fundraisers, and uses volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to accurately describe how the organization funds programs and why multiple revenue/partnership streams are necessary. Avoid implying programs are free or limitless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: empowerment and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame homeowners as gaining 'strength, stability and independence' through partnership, and emphasize preparation for responsibilities of homeownership (personal finances, mortgages, maintenance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight financial education and training as part of the mission. Use language that underscores empowerment, skill-building, and long-term stability rather than charity or dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local scope and impact details
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing the organization, specify geographic service area (Clinton, Eaton, Ingham counties, Michigan) and relevant impact facts (35+ year history, direct services to over 1,000 families).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, local impact metrics to ground stories. Ensure any statistics are up-to-date and attributable to Habitat Capital Region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Habitat Capital Region social media accounts and handles (Facebook, Facebook ReStore, Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn) and provide press contact info (info@habitatcr.org and office phone (517) 374-1313).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links and handles to official accounts for verification and follow-up. Direct media and partners to email or call for questions; use the provided contact points for press inquiries.
